title: Building operators eager for coronavirus info as one Seattle tower closed Monday
summary: F5 Tower in Seattle was closed for one day due to coronavirus concerns after an employee had contact with someone who tested positive for the virus. This closure highlights the growing concern among building operators seeking information as authorities anticipate an increase in cases.

title: HPE Confirms Discover Conference Still On, Cancels ‘Most’ Events Through April
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has decided to proceed with its annual Discover Las Vegas and Discover More London conferences, despite canceling or postponing most other events through April due to coronavirus concerns. Partners have expressed support for HPE's decision, emphasizing the need to continue business while taking prudent precautions. The company plans to shift resources to digital engagement for customers and partners.

title: Target's online sales surge as shoppers opt for pick up, delivery
summary: Target announced a 20% surge in digital sales, driven by increased use of its pick-up and delivery services. The retailer plans to expand its online offerings to include perishables like milk, wine, and beer for drive-up pickup, and will also experiment with even smaller store formats. Target also addressed concerns regarding the coronavirus, stating its impact on performance is not notable, but they are preparing for potential supply chain delays.

title: Carlyle Group’s $1.4 Billion Folly: Inside The Biggest Buyout Loss In Washington, D.C. Firm’s 33-Year History
summary: Carlyle Group's $1.4 billion equity investment in Acosta was completely wiped out, marking the biggest buyout loss in the firm's 33-year history. Acosta, a food broker, faced declining revenues due to shifting consumer preferences and aggressive cost-cutting by clients, leading to a bankruptcy filing despite Carlyle's efforts. The article highlights the growing trend of private equity firms trading companies among themselves and the risks associated with high debt levels in such deals.

title: Lawmakers ask Amazon, EBay to crack down on counterfeit sales
summary: House lawmakers are urging Amazon.com Inc. and EBay Inc. to take stronger action against third-party vendors selling fake, stolen, or unsafe goods on their platforms. The bipartisan request follows concerns about organized retail crime and counterfeit products, especially those originating from China. Both Amazon and EBay executives testified that they are investing in tools and supporting law enforcement to combat fraudulent listings.

title: Theme Lab: A Look Inside An Amazon Fulfillment Center
summary: This article details a "Theme Lab" visit to an Amazon Fulfillment Center, showcasing how robotics, IoT, AI, and human labor collaborate in the Stowing, Picking, Packing, and Shipping phases. It highlights the critical synergistic roles of these technologies and human expertise in achieving efficiency in e-commerce fulfillment. The article concludes by discussing related ETFs that track these disruptive technologies.

title: Watch Jessica Alba Put Her Product Prowess to the Test in ELLE's Beauty Haul
summary: Jessica Alba, co-founder of The Honest Company and Honest Beauty, takes on ELLE's "Beauty Haul" challenge. She demonstrates her clean beauty routine, shopping for products with a $150 budget and applying a full face of makeup in under 30 minutes. Alba highlights her favorite Honest Beauty products and explains her approach to clean beauty, emphasizing natural ingredients and avoiding fragrances.

title: Alliance Data: Is Three a Charm with a New CEO?
summary: Alliance Data, a private label credit card company, is facing significant challenges, including a ten-year stock low and rising charge-off rates, as a new CEO, Ralph Andretta, takes the helm. The article highlights the company's reliance on proprietary credit scores instead of FICO, a lack of innovation compared to competitors like Synchrony, and the need for a strategy to convert weaker credit accounts to branded network cards. The new CEO has initiated a "listening tour" to develop a strategic plan for the struggling firm.

title: Costco sales surge 11% as coronavirus fear prompts stockpiling
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. reported an 11% surge in sales due to customer stockpiling of essentials amid coronavirus fears, forcing frequent replenishment of items. The company also exceeded holiday-quarter expectations with a 28% increase in e-commerce sales and strong membership revenue, while acknowledging the continued rise in traffic into March. Analyst Garrett Nelson of CFRA Research considers Costco a primary beneficiary of coronavirus-related consumer stockpiling.

title: Champion Jumps to Amazon From Target for Discount C9 Brand
summary: Champion, owned by Hanesbrands Inc., has moved its C9 apparel line to Amazon.com Inc. after its agreement with Target Corp. ended. Amazon has entered into a two-year deal to offer the C9 line, marking the first time C9 will be available globally.

title: Burlington Stores walks away from e-commerce
summary: Burlington Stores is winding down its e-commerce operations, citing the difficulty of making a profit on low-priced items online, the challenge of replicating the "treasure hunt" experience digitally, and the strong performance of its physical stores. This decision comes despite the growth of e-commerce in other retail sectors, as Burlington focuses its resources on brick-and-mortar growth. The move sparks debate among experts about its long-term implications for the off-price retailer.

title: NetApp sinks claws into Talon Storage
summary: NetApp has acquired Talon Storage, a company specializing in caching software that connects branch offices to public cloud file servers. The acquisition aims to provide a unified footprint for unstructured data, enabling seamless access for users regardless of their geographical location. Talon's FAST software will allow NetApp to offer an indirect remote office/branch office (ROBO) presence without requiring on-premises NetApp filers.

title: HanesBrands Launches Popular C9 Champion Brand With Amazon in Multiyear Exclusive Agreement
summary: HanesBrands has launched its popular C9 Champion performance athleticwear exclusively on Amazon Fashion worldwide through a multiyear agreement. The value-priced line, which includes activewear, innerwear, and accessories for the whole family, aims to reach a broader global consumer base and complement the existing mainline Champion brand on Amazon.

title: Costco tells office workers
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is requiring its head office employees in Issaquah to report to work, despite public health requests to allow remote work. CEO W. Craig Jelinek stated that this decision is based on equity and fairness, as the majority of Costco employees work in stores and warehouses and do not have the option to work from home. This contrasts with companies like Amazon and Microsoft, which have allowed many office workers to work remotely amid coronavirus concerns.

title: Starbucks stores may go drive-thru only or limit seating to address coronavirus concerns
summary: Starbucks announced that some of its stores in the U.S. and Canada might transition to drive-thru only or limit seating to address concerns about the coronavirus pandemic. The company plans to make these decisions on a store-by-store basis and may temporarily close stores as a last resort. Starbucks has also expanded catastrophe pay for employees affected by the virus, and its shares have significantly dropped amid the outbreak.

title: Zero-Day Bug In Verisign And IaaS Services Allowed Registering of Malicious Domains With Homoglyph
summary: A zero-day bug found in Verisign and various IaaS services allowed cybercriminals to register malicious domains using homoglyphs, making them appear visually identical to legitimate sites. A researcher exposed the flaw, which had been actively exploited since 2017, and successfully registered imposter domains for major companies. While Verisign and Amazon have implemented mitigations, other services have yet to address the vulnerability.

title: Synchrony Financial agrees to 10-year deal to stay in Kettering
summary: Synchrony Financial, a major employer in Kettering, has secured a 10-year agreement to remain in the Kettering Business Park. The city extended a $675,000 Economic Development Incentive Grant for a five-year lease with a five-year option, with the company committing to maintain 1,900 full-time equivalent positions. This deal highlights Synchrony's significance to the local economy and the city's efforts to retain key businesses.

title: Bill Gates steps down from Microsoft board
summary: Bill Gates announced he is stepping down from the boards of Microsoft and Berkshire Hathaway to dedicate more time to philanthropy, focusing on global health, education, and climate change through the Gates Foundation. He will continue to serve as a technology advisor to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Gates, who co-founded Microsoft in 1975, remains one of the world's richest individuals.

title: WeRide resumes robotaxi service in China after COVID-19
summary: WeRide, an L4 AV smart mobility company based in Guangzhou, China, has resumed its robotaxi service with strict precautions after COVID-19. The company has implemented measures such as nucleic acid tests for safety drivers, daily health checks, mandatory mask-wearing, and vehicle sanitization after every two trips to ensure the safety of riders and drivers. WeRide, which partners with Amazon's AWS, emphasizes its R&D and claims to have one of the largest autonomous vehicle fleets among Chinese startups, having covered over 1,150,000 kilometers.

title: Amazon to hire 100,000 workers as online orders surge on coronavirus worries
summary: Amazon.com Inc announced plans to hire 100,000 warehouse and delivery workers in the United States to manage a significant increase in online orders due to the coronavirus outbreak. The company will also add $2 to its minimum $15 per hour wage for U.S. workers through April, an initiative expected to cost over $350 million across North America and Europe. Other retailers are also seeking new hires as consumers shift to online shopping and stock up on essential goods.

title: Canadian Solar secures €55m financing to build 151MW solar projects in Italy
summary: Canadian Solar has secured €55m ($60.6m) in financing from Intesa Sanpaolo for the construction of a 151MW portfolio of 12 solar projects in Italy. These projects, located in Sicily, Apulia, and Lazio, are expected to generate 287GWh of clean energy annually and are among the country's first subsidy-free utility-scale solar plants. The company also recently signed a PPA with Amazon for its Gunnedah solar plant in Australia.

title: Coconut water is the pandemic’s newest shortage
summary: Amid coronavirus concerns, sales of coconut water, particularly from Vita Coco, have surged significantly across the U.S., depleting typical stockpiles and straining supply chains. While other bottled waters are also in high demand, this trend raises concerns about potential supply disruptions if borders close, especially since coconuts are not grown in the US.

title: Broadcom Asserts Patents Covering ‘Crucial Aspects’ of Netflix Content Delivery
summary: Broadcom Corporation has filed a patent infringement lawsuit against Netflix, Inc. in the Central District of California, alleging that Netflix's streaming service infringes on nine of Broadcom's U.S. patents. The patents cover technologies crucial for reliable content delivery, efficient server use, and video encoding. Broadcom claims Netflix's infringement has harmed its set-top box business by drawing consumers away from cable television.

title: Reese Witherspoon’s Draper James and Land’s End Dive Into Swimwear
summary: Reese Witherspoon’s Draper James brand partnered with Land's End to launch a limited-edition women's swimwear collection. The collaboration combines Draper James' signature Southern-inspired prints with Land’s End's swim expertise, offering 23 pieces in sizes XS-3X. A portion of the proceeds from the collection will be donated to Girls Inc.

title: Marcus Corp. operates cinemas, hotels and restaurants. Here's how it's weathering the coronavirus pandemic.
summary: Marcus Corp., encompassing hotels and movie theaters, has been severely impacted by the coronavirus pandemic. CEO Greg Marcus is focused on financially preserving the company and supporting laid-off employees while navigating the unprecedented economic shock. Despite the challenges, Marcus believes the company's conservative financial approach will help it survive until business returns to normal.

title: Conduent Collaborates with Amazon Web Services to Help Government Agencies Scale Their COVID-19 Response
summary: Conduent announced that its Maven disease surveillance platform, configured for COVID-19 case management, patient outreach, and contact tracing visualization, is now available on Amazon Web Services (AWS). To support public health agencies, Conduent is waiving the software license fee for the Maven COVID-19 module through June 30, 2020, for qualified state and territorial-level agencies. This collaboration enables rapid and scalable deployment of critical tools to help "flatten the curve" by digitizing contact tracing and reporting.

title: Chipotle joins Starbucks, Amazon with coronavirus pay bump
summary: Chipotle announced a 10 percent pay increase for its hourly employees working between March 16 and April 12, joining companies like Starbucks and Amazon in providing additional compensation during the coronavirus pandemic. This initiative, along with updated emergency benefits, aims to show appreciation for workers during a time when many businesses are shifting to takeout or delivery-only operations. Other companies, including Albertsons, Kroger, Walmart, and McDonald's, are also offering similar support to their employees.

title: Maintaining a high-speed connection: A new playbook for cable growth
summary: This article outlines strategies for the cable industry to maintain growth, focusing on becoming a digital-first enterprise, doubling down on B2B growth, and becoming a leading smart-home player. It highlights the industry's strong current position while addressing looming long-term challenges such as regulatory risks and 5G competition. The authors emphasize the importance of strategic shifts to avoid becoming a "dumb pipe" and to continue increasing the value of customer relationships.

title: Social Media Moves to New Era of Growth
summary: Social media platforms are entering a new era of growth, shifting focus from user acquisition to maximizing revenue per user through targeted advertising and innovative technologies. New avenues like social commerce and AR/VR are being explored to diversify revenue streams. This evolution includes in-app purchases, live-streaming commerce, and augmented reality experiences to further engage users and drive monetization.
